Every public and protected member reviewed. Returns the cosine, not the angle - no acos appears in the source. The f32 reduction of Eigen's SparseVector<float>::dot is reproduced exactly (ascending index order, widened once), as is the sqrt(sum1 * sum2) grouping, which is what makes self-similarity exactly 1.0. The source's own empty/all-zero guard (sum1 * sum2 == 0 returns 0.0) is kept verbatim, and the score is not clamped, so a spectrum against its negation scores -1.0. Deliberately not ported: the empty updateMembers_ and the dead precursor_mass_tolerance_. Native: incompatible binning is a checked Error::InvalidValue where the source only asserts through OPENMS_PRECONDITION, a release-build no-op unlike both siblings; f32 dot-product overflow is a checked error; MAX_COMPARED_BINS bounds the comparison.

Every public and protected member reviewed. The agreement rule is ported literally: per bin (a + b) * 0.5 - |a - b|, truncated at zero, summed, over the mean of the two totals, capped at 1.0. The walk spans the union of the stored bins because sparse addition does, the arithmetic stays f32 (Eigen promotes the scalar 0.5 down to float), and cwiseMax(0) semantics are written out rather than using f32::max. Deliberately not ported: the empty updateMembers_ and the dead precursor_mass_tolerance_. Native: a zero mean total yields 0.0 where the source returns NaN or 1.0; incompatible binning is Error::InvalidValue; f32 overflow is checked; MAX_COMPARED_BINS bounds the comparison. (1) Every NaN the FileInfo text layer prints is spelled nan, where glibc spells a NaN whose sign bit is set -nan. The consensusXML -s blocks are the first FileInfo path whose own arithmetic can produce a NaN at all -- FileInfo.cpp:2310 divides and :2312-2315 inverts every ratio below 1, so a sub-feature of intensity 0 under a positive centroid contributes 1/0 = +inf and one of intensity -0.0 contributes -inf -- and any of the seven value lines a SummaryStatistics block prints (the mean, the five order statistics and the variance) can therefore carry one. The VALUE is reproduced: both builds compute 0xfff8000000000000 on x86_64, measured with argv-fed probes so nothing is constant-folded. Making the sign printable is carried forward as its own wave. (2) A SummaryStatistics sample holding both a negative and a positive zero is ordered by the IEEE-754 total order here and left in file order by the source's std::sort, which calls -0.0 and 0.0 equivalent. FileInfo.cpp:2310-2311 fills the Intensity ratios sample BEFORE the inversion, so one consensus feature with sub-features of intensity -0.0 and 0.0 puts both into it; the strict-weak-ordering precondition HOLDS there, nothing is undefined, and only the permutation is unspecified, but minimum, the quartiles and maximum are positional reads and ostream writes -0 for a negative zero. sort_ascending uses f64::total_cmp, which puts -0.0 first, so the port prints one of the two answers for both file orders. Measured in both: a7_cons_nan_one.consensusXML and a7_cons_zero_swapped.consensusXML hold the same consensus feature with its two sub-feature intensities exchanged and their Release reports disagree on exactly those four lines. Accepted rather than refused, because refusing would widen a refusal in shared math to an input the Release build handles in bounds and stably; recorded as native difference 6 and pinned by consensus_a_signed_zero_sample_is_ordered_by_the_total_order. One boundary is deferred rather than ported, and is raised for the lead (CPP-347). The same arithmetic can put a NaN into the statistics SAMPLE: a consensus feature with one sub-feature of intensity -0.0 and one of 0.0 contributes (-inf) + (+inf) at :2317, which :2323 divides by cm.size() and :2327 pushes into it_aad_by_cfs. Math::SummaryStatistics then hands that sample to std::sort. Under operator< a NaN is incomparable with every value, itself included, so std::sort may return any permutation of the elements it cannot tell apart -- and with two or more distinct numbers present the strict-weak-ordering precondition fails outright. SummaryStatistics::new reproduces the two shapes whose set of possible outputs has one member -- a one-value sample, which has exactly one permutation, and an all-NaN sample, every permutation of which prints the same eight lines (oracle cases c_nan_one{,_s,_all} and c_nan_two{,_s}, all reproduced) -- and refuses a NaN next to a number. Measured: c_nan_then_finite_s and c_finite_then_nan_s hold the same two consensus features in opposite file order and disagree on exactly those four lines. All public members reviewed and documented. eval, num_interior_knots, rss and smoothing_param are ported; ok() is expressed as the Result from the constructors rather than as a method that could only return true. The class does not solve the penalised problem its own header describes: it tries a cubic polynomial first, accepts it within a ten-percent margin of the residual budget, and only then searches the fixed node list 4, 6, 8, n/2, 3n/4, n. src/openms/include/OpenMS/MATH/MISC/Cubi.scope: All five public members reviewed and documented. Both constructors, eval and derivatives are ported; the C++ derivative(x) and derivatives(x, order) overloads collapse into one derivative(x, order) because the former's body is literally the latter. The map constructor becomes from_pairs, reproducing std::map's sort and first-value-wins key collapse so the deduplicated size check matches. The Burden/Faires recurrence is transcribed term by term in its original evaluation order. The natural boundary condition was confirmed from CubicSpline2d.cpp:152 and the recurrence, and is asserted as exact zero at both ends. Port is stricter in two documented places: it rejects repeated and non-finite abscissae, which the C++ accepts (its check is only non-decreasing) and then turns into NaN coefficients, and it rejects non-finite query positions, which the C++ indexes one past the end of its knot vector. MAX_POINTS is a native ceiling. Native peak_maximum is retained for the peak picker and marked as not a port of this header. Evidence tier 2, bit-for-bit against an executed probe; all 4 class-test sections mapped. perf/spline-scratch (wave 4) adds CubicSpline2dFitter, a caller-owned scratch that replaces the eight heap vectors CubicSpline2d::with_max_points allocated per constructed spline (h, mu, z, b, c, d and the two input copies). The recurrence is unchanged term by term and in its original evaluation order, so the coefficients are bit-identical by construction; SplineFunction is now implemented for &T so existing callers still compile. The picker constructs one spline per centroid - 22,776,198 on the benchmark run - and alloc::alloc was 271,144,136 of the 590,918,793 instructions the construction cost (46%). Measured with the fitter wired into the picker on the 2.3 GB input at one thread, 11 interleaved pairs: 33.19 s to 32.01 s wall (paired -1.27 s), pick phase 17.24 s to 15.11 s, output sha256 unchanged. The fitter is a local of pick_signal, so each rayon worker owns its own and there is no shared mutable state. This is a native addition to the header's surface, not a port of a C++ member; the two source constructors, eval and the derivatives are unchanged.
